dish.d: A vessel such as a plate for holding or serving food, often flat with a depressed region in the middle.

do.e: We’re having a bit of a do on Saturday to celebrate my birthday.

doctor.d: A physician; a member of the medical profession; one who is trained and licensed to heal the sick or injured. The final examination and qualification may award a doctor degree in which case the post-nominal letters are D.O., DPM, M.D., DMD, DDS, in the US or MBBS in the UK.
doctor.e: If you still feel unwell tomorrow, see your doctor.

does.e: All you ever do is surf the Internet. What will you do this afternoon?

dog.d: A mammal, Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris, that has been domesticated for thousands of years, of highly variable appearance due to human breeding.
dog.e: The dog barked all night long.

doing.e: This is his doing. (= "He did it.")

doll.d: A small figure resembling a human being that is used as a toy.

dollar.d: Official designation for currency in some parts of the world, including Canada, the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Hong Kong, and elsewhere. Its symbol is $.

door.d: A portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle, typically consisting of a rigid plane movable on a hinge. It may have a handle to help open and close, a latch to hold it closed, and a lock that ensures it cannot be opened without a key.
door.e: bathroom door, bedroom door, doorkey, exterior door, interior door

down.e: I love almost everything about my job. The only down is that I can't take Saturdays off.

dr.d: A person or firm that owes money; one in debt; one who owes a debt

drama.d: A composition, normally in prose, telling a story and intended to be represented by actors impersonating the characters and speaking the dialogue.
drama.e: The author released her latest drama, which became a best-seller.

draw.d: Senses relating to exerting force or pulling. To pull (someone or something) in a particular direction or manner.

dream.d: Imaginary events seen in the mind while sleeping.

dress.d: An item of clothing (usually worn by a woman or young girl) which both covers the upper part of the body and includes skirts below the waist.
dress.e: He came to the party in formal dress.

drink.d: To consume (a liquid) through the mouth.
drink.e: What kind of drink would you like? We have soft drinks and hard drinks.

drive.d: Motivation to do or achieve something; ability coupled with ambition.
drive.e: Crassus had wealth and wit, but Pompey had drive and Caesar as much again.

driver.d: One who drives something, in any sense of the verb to drive.

drop.d: A small quantity of liquid, just large enough to hold its own round shape via surface tension, especially one that falls from a source of liquid.
drop.e: asked for just a drop more tea; she was thirsty and there wasn't a drop of water to be found

drum.d: A percussive musical instrument spanned with a thin covering on at least one end for striking, forming an acoustic chamber, affecting what materials are used to make it; a membranophone.
drum.e: Replace the drum unit of your printer.

dry.e: This towel's dry. Could you wet it and cover the chicken so it doesn't go dry as it cooks?

due.e: Give him his due — he is a good actor.

each other.d: (reciprocal pronoun) To one another; one to the other; signifies that a verb applies to two or more entities both as subjects and as direct objects:
each other.e: Jack and Robert loved each other.

ear.d: The organ of hearing, consisting of the pinna, auditory canal, eardrum, malleus, incus, stapes and cochlea.

early.d: At a time in advance of the usual or expected event.
early.e: at eleven, we went for an early lunch;  she began reading at an early age;  his mother suffered an early death

easy.e: Now that I know it's taken care of, I can rest easy at night.

eat.d: Something to be eaten; a meal; a food item.

egg.d: An approximately spherical or ellipsoidal body produced by birds, insects, reptiles, and other animals, often housing an embryo within a membrane or shell during its development. The (usually) non-developing, edible egg (sense 1.1) of a domestic fowl such as a duck, goose, or, especially, chicken; the contents of such an egg or eggs used as food.
egg.e: We made a big omelette with three eggs for breakfast.

eight.d: A numerical value equal to 8; the number occurring after seven and before nine.
eight.e: He works eight hours a day.

eighteen.d: The cardinal number occurring after seventeen and before nineteen, represented in Roman numerals as XVIII and in Arabic numerals as 18.

eighty.d: The cardinal number occurring after seventy-nine and before eighty-one, represented in Roman numerals as LXXX and in Arabic numerals as 80.

either.e: I don't like him, and I don't like her either.

elementary.d: Relating to the basic, essential or fundamental part of something.
elementary.e: At Lakeside Elementary I learned to appreciate the forest.

eleven.d: The cardinal number occurring after ten and before twelve. Represented as 11 in Arabic digits.

else.d: (used only with indefinite or interrogative pronouns) Other; in addition to previously mentioned items.
else.e: The instructor is busy. Can anyone else help me?

email.d: A system for transferring messages from one computer to another, usually through a network.
email.e: He sent me his details via email.

end.d: The terminal point of something in space or time.
end.e: At the end of the road, turn left.

engineer.d: A soldier engaged in designing or constructing military works for attack or defence, or other engineering works. A soldier in charge of operating a weapon; an artilleryman, a gunner.

enjoy.d: To receive pleasure or satisfaction from something.
enjoy.e: Enjoy your holidays!   I very much enjoy dancing.

evening.d: The time of the day between dusk and night, when it gets dark.

event.e: I went to an event in San Francisco last week.

every.d: All of a countable group (considered individually), without exception.
every.e: Every person in the room stood and cheered.

everybody.d: Every individual in a set; all people.
everybody.e: Does everybody have their ticket(s) at hand?

everyday.d: Appropriate for ordinary use, rather than for special occasions.
everyday.e: Putting away the tableware for everyday, a chore which is part of the everyday.

everyone.d: Every individual in a set; every person.

everything.e: I checked the list again and everything is done.

everywhere.d: In or to all locations under discussion.
everywhere.e: He delivers the mail everywhere on this street.

example.d: Something that is representative of all such things in a group.

excited.d: Having great enthusiasm, passion and energy.
excited.e: He was very excited about his promotion.

exciting.e: The fireworks which opened the festivities excited anyone present.

excuse.d: Explanation designed to avoid or alleviate guilt or negative judgment; a plea offered in extenuation of a fault.
excuse.e: Tell me why you were late – and I don't want to hear any excuses!

exercise.d: Any activity designed to develop or hone a skill or ability.
exercise.e: The teacher told us that the next exercise is to write an essay.

expensive.d: Given to expending a lot of money; profligate, lavish.

eye.d: An organ through which animals see (“perceive surroundings via light”).
eye.e: The car was quite pleasing to the eye, but impractical.

face.d: The front part of the head of a human or other animal, featuring the eyes, nose and mouth, and the surrounding area.
face.e: That girl has a pretty face.

factory.d: A trading establishment, especially set up by merchants working in a foreign country.
factory.e: See how there's another layer of metal there? That's not factory.

fair.d: Something which is fair (in various senses of the adjective).
fair.e: When will we learn to distinguish between the fair and the foul?

fairy.d: A mythical being of human form with magical powers, known in many sizes and descriptions, although typically depicted as a small sprite with gauze-like wings, especially one that is female. Fairies are revered in some modern forms of paganism.

family.d: A group of people who are closely related to one another (by blood, marriage or adoption); kin; for example, a set of parents and their children; an immediate family.

famous.d: To make famous; to bring renown to.
famous.e: Some people are only famous within their city.

fan.d: A hand-held device consisting of concertinaed material, or slats of material, gathered together at one end, that may be opened out into the shape of a sector of a circle and waved back and forth in order to move air towards oneself and cool oneself.
fan.e: We enjoyed standing at the edge of the cliff, being fanned by the wind.

farm.d: A place where agricultural and similar activities take place, especially the growing of crops or the raising of livestock.
farm.e: Farm out the stable and pigsty.

farmer.d: A person who works the land and/or who keeps livestock, especially on a farm.

fast.d: Firmly or securely fixed in place; stable.
fast.e: That rope is dangerously loose. Make it fast!

fat.d: Carrying more fat than usual on one's body; plump; not lean or thin.
fat.e: The fat man had problems going through the door.

father.d: A male parent, especially of a human; a male who parents a child (which he has sired, adopted, fostered, etc.).
father.e: My father was a strong influence on me.

favourite.d: Most-liked. (In other words, [person]'s favorite [noun] = the [noun] that [person] likes the most.)

feed.e: They sell feed, riding helmets, and everything else for horses.

feel.d: A quality of an object experienced by touch.

feeling.d: (heading) To use or experience the sense of touch.
feeling.e: The wool on my arm produced a strange feeling.

festival.d: An event or community gathering, usually staged by a local community, which centers on some theme, sometimes on some unique aspect of the community.

fever.d: A higher than normal body temperature of a person (or, generally, a mammal), usually caused by disease.
fever.e: "I have a fever. I think I've the flu."

field.d: A land area free of woodland, cities, and towns; open country.
field.e: There are several species of wild flowers growing in this field.

fifteen.d: The cardinal number occurring after fourteen (14) and before sixteen (16).

fifty.d: The cardinal number occurring after forty-nine and before fifty-one.
fifty.e: Do you want small bills or are fifties OK?

fight.d: To contend in physical conflict, either singly or in war, battle etc.
fight.e: A wounded animal will fight like a maniac, relentless, savage and murderous.

file.d: A collection of papers collated and archived together.
file.e: The troops marched in Indian file.

fill.d: To occupy fully, to take up all of.

find.d: Anything that is found (usually valuable), as objects on an archeological site or a person with talent.
find.e: I found my car keys. They were under the couch.

finish.d: An end; the end of anything.
finish.e: The car's finish was so shiny and new.

fire.d: A (usually self-sustaining) chemical reaction involving the bonding of oxygen with carbon or other fuel, with the production of heat and the presence of flame or smouldering.
fire.e: We sat about the fire singing songs and telling tales.

first.d: The person or thing in the first position.
first.e: He was the first to complete the course.

fish.d: A typically cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills; any vertebrate that is not a tetrapod.

fishing.e: We had a good day's fishing at the weekend.

five.d: A numerical value equal to 5; the number following four and preceding six.
five.e: He wrote a five followed by four zeroes.

flag.d: A piece of cloth, often decorated with an emblem, used as a visual signal or symbol.
flag.e: The flag of France has three vertical stripes.

flat.e: The land around here is flat.

floor.d: The interior bottom or surface of a house or building; the supporting surface of a room.
floor.e: The room has a wooden floor.

flower.d: A colorful, conspicuous structure associated with angiosperms, frequently scented and attracting various insects, and which may or may not be used for sexual reproduction.

fly.d: Any insect of the order Diptera; characterized by having two wings (except for some wingless species), also called true flies.

focus.d: A point at which reflected or refracted rays of light converge.
focus.e: The heat of sunlight at the focus of a magnifying glass can easily set dry leaves on fire.

foggy.d: Obscured by mist or fog; unclear; hazy
foggy.e: He was still foggy with sleep.

following.d: Coming next, either in sequence or in time.
